messages:
evan-support: Filing an urgent customer report from ACME — they see cache 'hits' returning embeddings with the wrong dimension after we switched their model to `open-embed-v2`.

The request returns an embedding length of 1536 but the cached payload is 768. Customer sees repeated 'hit' responses (fast) but the vector shape mismatch causes downstream errors. Ticket #C-8893. Repro steps below.

jordan-ml: Can you paste the exact request + headers + any request_id from the responses? Also confirm tenant id and whether they use our prefixing header or rely on automatic tenant keying. :eyes:

evan-support: Repro curl we used:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Tenant: acme-corp" \
  -H "X-Embed-Prefix: user:acme/v1" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-v2","input":"hello world"}'
```

Response (cached, very quick):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-cache: HIT
content: {"embedding": [ /* 768 floats */ ] }
```

But when we force `cache_bypass=true` we get:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-cache: MISS
content: {"embedding": [ /* 1536 floats */ ] }
```

jordan-ml: Interesting. So the same request (same tenant + same model) yields a HIT with 768 and MISS with 1536. That screams keying/prefix when prefetch or older model variant used a different embedding size. Do we know if ACME was recently migrated from `open-embed-v1` -> `v2`?

maria-eng: They were migrated last week as part of a staged rollout. Two hypotheses: 1) prefetch/cache-warm path used a legacy global prefix key (no tenant), or 2) a background batch job populated keys for the old model variant and our key scheme doesn't include model version in all code paths. Both can cause shadow hits.

Can infra share cache lookup logs for a couple of the fast hits and the miss? Need the exact cache keys.

infra-bot: Retrieved logs for thread. Sample lines (sanitized):

```
[2176543223] cache:get key="emb:global:sha1:4f2d..." result=HIT size=6144
[2176543223] cache:get key="emb:tenant:acme-corp:model:open-embed-v2:sha1:9a7b..." result=MISS
[2176543250] cache:get key="emb:tenant:acme-corp:model:open-embed-v2:sha1:9a7b..." result=MISS
[2176543251] cache:get key="emb:global:sha1:4f2d..." result=HIT size=3072
```

nora-ops: Those logs line up with maria's hypotheses — prefetch appears to have stored a global-scoped key (no tenant/model suffix) that corresponds to the old 768-dim embedding (size=3072 bytes ~= 768*4). Runtime reads tenant-scoped key for fresh compute but the quick path returns global key hits.

Immediate repro I recommend for support to confirm:
- Call with `X-Embed-Prefix` toggled off vs on
- Toggle `?cache_prefetch=false` in the request URL
- Compare `x-cache` header and response time

Workaround for ACME: explicitly set `X-Embed-Cache-Key: tenant:acme-corp:model:open-embed-v2` or disable prefetch on their account for now.

jordan-ml: I'll open a runtime ticket to lock down the prefetch key namespace so it always includes tenant+model. Action items:
- eng-runtime: patch prefetch key generation (include tenant + model version) — high
- eng-ml: run bulk scan for global keys matching common phrases used in on-boarding (to estimate blast radius)
- support/ops: keep ACME on bypass or set explicit key as nora suggested

evan-support: Customer is on paid tier and hitting production exceptions on their service. Can we get an ETA on the runtime patch and a short term mitigation? They requested a hotfix or config toggle.

maria-eng: I'll take runtime patch, can do a targeted rollback/hotfix for prefetch in the next 6-8 hours if infra approves. Short-term mitigation: toggle prefetch off for ACME via feature flag or add per-tenant enforced keying in the proxy layer.

nora-ops: I'll open a feature-flag ticket and apply to ACME account now. Also will run the toggle repro and paste results to ticket.

evan-support: Thanks — please @jordan-ml @maria-eng when patch lands, and I'll notify the customer. :+1:

jordan-ml: Adding one more note — include a small repro harness in the runtime PR that runs across `open-embed-v1` and `v2` variants to confirm no cross-variant key overlap. Saves us any surprises on future rollouts. :thumbsup:

evan-support: Will keep the ticket updated with customer test results. Closing loop once hotfix is in prod.
